questions.question: What happens when the React Compiler finds a component that mutates its props?
options: It rewrites the code to clone the props
It throws an error at runtime
It skips optimising that component and leaves it as written
questions.explanation: The compiler relies on the Rules of React. When it detects a violation it bails out of that component rather than risk changing behaviour.

questions.question: Why should you profile a production or profiling build rather than a development build?
options: Development builds include extra checks that make timings much slower and misleading
The Profiler tab does not exist in development
questions.explanation: Development mode adds warnings and checks, so render times don't reflect what users experience.

questions.question: In the Profiler component's onRender callback, what does baseDuration represent?
options: The time the browser spent painting
The time since the app started
An estimate of re-rendering the whole subtree without any memoisation
The network time to load the component
questions.explanation: actualDuration is the time spent this commit; baseDuration estimates the full subtree cost. A big gap shows memoisation is helping.

questions.question: Which Core Web Vital is most directly affected by slow React rendering in response to user input?
questions.explanation: Interaction to Next Paint measures how quickly the page responds to interactions, which long renders and hydration work delay.
